messages:
darya: Quick question — packaging guidance for quant profiles we plan to push to Redwood Optimize. How strict should semver be for profile bundles? e.g. `qpack-llama2-13b-awq-v1.0.0` vs `qpack-llama2-13b-awq-1`
oscar: I vote for semantic-ish: major.minor.patch. Major = breaking change in inference contract, minor = new safe optimizations, patch = metadata/typo fixes. keeps compatibility clear.
kevin: Agree. Also add a `schema_version` inside the manifest so runtime can reject incompatible bundles at load.
darya: Good call. What should go in the manifest? names, model hash, quant_type, hardware hint, expected seq_len distribution?
mika: Minimal manifest I use locally: `profile_name`, `schema_version`, `model_id`, `model_commit`, `quant_backend` (AWQ/GPTQ/INT8/FP8), `ops_compat` (list of ops), `hw_tags` (e.g., a100,h100), `seq_len_hint`, `quality_delta_pct`, `fallback_profiles`
kevin: + `consumer_compat` or `consumer_names` — how services should reference it (e.g., chat-service, embedder). we had issues where a profile was applied to reranker and produced bad deltas.
darya: On quality_delta_pct — what's the guidance for thresholds to block rollout? we need to be conservative.
oscar: We gate minor releases if any eval set shows >1% relative drop in Accuracy@k or >2% MRR drop. Patch releases ok for <0.1% noise. But these numbers should be configurable per consumer.
mika: Also include an automated `delta_report` artifact link in the bundle: CI should produce a small CSV/markdown with evals vs baseline across priority prompt sets.
kevin: For runtime fallback, include `fallback_profiles` order and a `cost_hint` (e.g., tokens/usd) so Optimize can route by cost/latency.
darya: Packaging format: tar.gz with `manifest.json`, `profile.json` (runtime rules), `eval_report.md`, and optional `tests/` with synthetic prompts. Do we compress or put on registry as JSON blobs?
oscar: Registry should store as immutable objects with content-addressed IDs + human-friendly semver tag. Upload bot can post link.
build-bot: Uploaded bundle `qpack-llama2-13b-awq-v1.0.0` to staging registry at https://artifacts.internal/redwood/qpacks/sha256:abc123 :rocket:
kevin: Nice. CI should validate manifest.schema_version matches runtime loader and run smoke inference on a small prompt set in staging.
mika: Naming conventions for consumer visibility: `qpack::<model_id>::<quant_backend>::vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` e.g. `qpack::llama2-13b::AWQ::v1.0.0` — easy to parse.
darya: Any objections to reserving `major` bump for ABI/IO format changes (like changing how KV cache keys are decoded)?
oscar: Definitely reserve major for ABI. Minor for algorithm tweaks (new calibration, different quant params that are runtime-compatible)
kevin: One more runtime thing: profiles should include `compat_matrix` mapping runtime versions to pass/fail, like `redwood-runtime>=2.5,<3.0` or a list of tested runtime SHAs.
mika: We'll also need a migration playbook in the bundle when major version changes — steps for rolling back if quality regressions crop up.
darya: Action: oscar to draft short RFC with manifest schema + semver policy. kevin to add CI smoke test template. mika to draft eval_report template with metrics we trust. I'll follow up with rollout thresholds per consumer. :+1:
oscar: On it. Draft by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
kevin: I'll PR the smoke test into `eng-ml/ci-qa`.
build-bot: Noted: staging bundle link pinned in #eng-ml.
darya: Thanks team — keeping this packaging clean will save ops headaches when Optimize starts recommending bundles at scale.
